summary: Critical auth/RBAC security fixes and hardening across the shared infrastructure and both SPAs. Root cause: five callers used GetByUnique(ctx,"","id",id) to look up users and roles by primary key, but no entity tags Id with ukey:"id", so SelectByUnique matched no filter and issued an unfiltered LIMIT 1 query, silently returning the first DB row — the stock superadmin. Every user and role lookup therefore resolved as superadmin, giving all users superadmin-level access. Fixes: SelectByUnique now fails closed when the key group matches no struct field (sqlite + postgres adapters); genericRepo.GetById and GetByUnique return (nil, nil) on not-found instead of a zero-value struct; five callers switched to repo.GetById (accessRoleService.GetById, userLoginResolver.ResolveAccessUser, userLoginService.Update + ChangePassword, controlUserService.GetById); regression test added. Additional hardening: (1) Role is now dynamic — AccessSessionMidware re-stamps claims.RoleId from the live user store on every request and IsSuperadmin resolves live, so role changes take effect immediately without re-login; the session role-mismatch check that bounced users to login on every role change is removed. (2) RequireSuperadmin middleware added and applied to /api/user-credential, /api/user-group (myidsan) and /api/rbac/users (myseliasan), making these surfaces superadmin-only regardless of matrix grants. (3) Self-role-change guarded in both apps. (4) New federated users provisioned with no role (pending) instead of viewer; viewer's legacy GET /api wildcard stripped on startup by EnsureViewerDefaults. (5) Node proxy/media/access APIs resolve the caller's live role on every request. (6) Superadmin short-circuit added to node access resolution. (7) New GET /api/nodes/access?roleId= endpoint for the central RBAC node-access matrix (superadmin only). (8) ListForRole sorts by Path ASC for stable RBAC matrix UI. Frontend: shared in-repo React module (frontend/shared/: DataTable, Toast/ToastStack, SideNav, icons) consumed by both apps via @shared webpack alias; per-app duplicates deleted. Three themes: Light, Dark, High Contrast. Side-nav follows the active theme via --nav-* tokens. PendingClearanceScreen in both SPAs. Nodes tree side-nav in myseliasan with expandable fleet listing. ManagedNode gained Description and Icon fields; AdoptInput.Name now wins over hostname.
compatibility: Existing installs: the viewer role's GET /api wildcard is stripped on startup (the first boot after this update removes it silently). Any role that relied on that blanket grant must have its permissions explicitly re-configured via /api/access-rbac/permissions. New federated logins in myseliasan get no role (pending) instead of viewer — a superadmin must assign a role before the user can access the control plane. Session role-mismatch in the session cache is no longer a reason to invalidate an active session; existing sessions remain valid through role changes (this is the intended behavior). The shared frontend module (frontend/shared/) is a new directory that must be present for the webpack build to succeed in both apps; it is tracked in the repo with no build step required. The ManagedNode Description and Icon columns are additive; existing adopted nodes default to empty strings and are unaffected operationally.
